heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock next-generation visual production with Seedream 4.5 for image generation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for video generation—advanced foundation models for professional creative teams.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed brand-orange hero with a translucent glass overlay and editorial collage treatment rather than a split layout. Keep the headline oversized and dramatic, with a dominant logo-proof bar directly beneath the CTA. The primary visual should be represented through layered product UI shells, abstract generative frames, and motion strips instead of a single hero image. Add premium mesh-gradient movement, subtle grid lines, and floating chips to signal enterprise-grade creative tooling. The hero should feel cinematic, controlled, and production-ready, with orange driving both the background and CTA emphasis.

repetitionBreakers: Hero is full-bleed orange with layered editorial collage
Trust is an early dominant logo bar immediately after hero
Product sections alternate between accordion-led and dark cinematic showcase
Pricing is split into two differentiated cards instead of a generic table
Testimonials switch to carousel to avoid another static grid
Final CTA is a floating conversion card to close with visual contrast
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation for Creative Teams
blueprint.metaDescription: Generate high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Built for creative directors, video producers, marketers, and enterprise visual teams.

sections.backgroundTreatment: solid brand-orange field with translucent glass overlay, floating capability chips, editorial sample frames, and subtle mesh-gradient motion texture
sections.designNote: Dynamic above-the-fold hero that answers what this is, who it is for, and what to do next. Use the ad message continuity: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for professional image and video creation. Keep the CTA as a single solid accent button labeled 'Get started' and make it visually dominant. Add a short benefit list under the subheadline, but keep the composition content-forward and premium, not overbuilt.

Logos-first trust treatment using 3-6 recognisable brand logos in a prominent horizontal strip directly after the hero. If exact logos are unavailable, use a polished logo-style metrics strip, but the preferred pattern is a marquee-like showcase to signal enterprise credibility early.

Split into two distinct product blocks with alternating visual rhythm. First block: Seedream 4.5 as the main spotlight with an accordion feature stack and a preview panel showing image-generation, editing, composition, and typography use cases. Second block: Seedance 1.5 Pro shifts into a darker cinematic contrast section with motion-first storytelling, emphasizing audio-visual sync, lip-sync, camera control, and speed. Because each product has 5+ features, use accordion behavior instead of a flat grid. Keep the layouts clearly different from each other and from the hero.

A compact credibility/support section using simple cards or counters. Even though no dedicated why-techjockey content is provided, this area should frame procurement confidence: enterprise-ready infrastructure, guided evaluation, and production-grade buying support. Keep it lighter and more utilitarian than the product blocks.

Present the two plans as stacked premium cards rather than a table. Highlight Seedance pricing and keep Seedream as request-quote style positioning. Use strong hierarchy, clear inclusions, and a single bold 'Get started' CTA on each card. Make this section more conversion-led without becoming crowded.

With 5 testimonials, use a carousel to keep the section elegant and avoid another dense card grid. Prioritize quotes from creative directors, video producers, and art directors to reinforce role-specific proof. Keep the visual treatment restrained, with one featured quote at a time and minimal chrome.

Final conversion block should feel like a premium floating card against a softer background. Keep it simple, high-clarity, and mobile-friendly. The only button text remains 'Get started', and on mobile it must be full-width. This section should feel like the cleanest path from evaluation to action.

Use this as a compact footer-adjacent credibility strip or closing band, not as a generic news section. Keep it subtle and utility-driven so the page ends with a polished brand-safe finish rather than a noisy content dump.

blueprint.designPersonality: An intelligent creative marketplace page: orange-led, editorial, and trust-heavy, combining premium motion graphics with enterprise proof. It should feel like a sophisticated AI production suite for serious visual teams, not a consumer demo or a generic software landing page.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a premium editorial hero collage: abstract AI visual frames, layered product UI shells, sample image thumbnails, waveform/video motion strips, and floating capability chips. Keep the logo trust bar dominant directly under the hero. Use SVG for trust logos and feature icons, PNG for product UI shells, and JPEG only for any large cinematic visual panel.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and needs to hold on a single elegant rhythm without breaking the layout, so a smaller premium display size is more balanced.

colours.colourReason: Brand primary orange is used as the hero background and primary CTA color per rule, while the rest of the system stays neutral and premium with white, near-black, and soft grey surfaces to keep the visual identity tied to Techjockey rather than a generic AI palette.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Split introductory hero with strong brand/logo presence, large headline, concise supporting copy, and a short benefit list; content is left-aligned and above-the-fold focused.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column hero followed by form-led conversion block and then feature/content sections; rhythm favors compact content blocks separated by clear vertical spacing rather than dense multi-column storytelling.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple boxed panels with solid backgrounds, modest borders/shadows implied by container separation, and utility-driven layout rather than decorative glass effects.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA-first approach with one dominant action near the hero and a secondary demo/request action in product sections; CTAs are button-like, direct, and conversion-oriented.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: Not enough reference evidence for a pricing module pattern from the provided HTML snippet.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not visible in provided markup; no extractable footer pattern.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible snippet; logo/brand image in the hero and icon-led bullets, with no prominent video/image gallery pattern present.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Feature sections should be modular and label-led, using a section name, short headline, description, and a compact feature list; structure supports progressive disclosure and scanning.
referenceMap.formPattern: Lead capture form appears as a distinct conversion card with a bold title, hidden metadata fields, and a stacked field area; optimized for business inquiry flows rather than checkout.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit motion system is evident in the provided HTML; if implemented, keep animation subtle and utility-based.
designNotes: Treat the page as a high-conversion B2B landing page with clear information hierarchy.
Prefer concise, scannable copy blocks and strong section boundaries.
Use consistent containers and generous vertical spacing to separate the hero, form, and feature content.
Keep imagery functional and brand-reinforcing rather than decorative.
Optimize for trust and lead capture rather than entertainment or deep navigation.

blueprint.additionalInstructions: PROOF STRATEGY: The visitor trusts logos most. Make this the dominant trust signal.

mustHaveMoments: Dominant logo/trust strip near the top above or beside the hero copy
Clear split hero with concise value proposition and primary CTA
Fast scan product modules for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro
Comparison-friendly pricing/quote blocks with direct request actions
Testimonial proof from relevant creative roles (director, producer, art director, marketer)
avoidPatterns: Badge-heavy trust treatment without recognizable logos
Long-form editorial storytelling before showing product capability
Overly decorative or futuristic visuals that reduce clarity
Dense technical explanation without a business outcome framing
Multiple competing CTAs in the hero
designStrategy.reasoning: This page should behave like a high-intent lead-generation landing page for a solution-aware audience evaluating advanced AI visual tools. The strongest trust signal is logos, so trust architecture should be logo-led and placed immediately in the first screen area. A split hero works best because it supports quick comprehension: message on one side, trust/proof and CTA on the other. The page should stay product-led because the user needs to understand what Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro do, but the conversion mechanism should be strong and direct, with quote/demo actions repeated in the product and pricing sections. The visual tone should feel premium and confident rather than playful, and the layout should remain balanced to preserve scanability across two products and testimonial proof.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
